nodes.name: Aerospace aluminum-lithium plate/sheet
nodes.description: Low-density, high-stiffness aluminum-lithium (Al-Li) rolled plate, sheet and extrusions used for launch-vehicle tank barrels, domes, intertanks, stage adapters and thrust structures. Falcon 9's stage structure is an aluminum-lithium alloy; Al-Li is the merchant material tier feeding reusable-launch tankage industry-wide. Qualified Al-Li capacity is scarce enough that OEMs sign decade-long lock-ins.
nodes.notes: Industry-framed: Constellium's Airware Al-Li is supplied to Blue Origin's New Glenn launch vehicle (public). SpaceX's specific Al-Li mill supplier for Falcon 9 tankage is not publicly disclosed in reviewed sources; the merchant Al-Li tier (Constellium, Kaiser, Arconic) is the investable exposure.

nodes.name: Aerospace mill titanium (plate/bar/billet)
nodes.description: Aerospace-grade titanium mill products (plate, bar, billet, forged stock) used for reentry-control surfaces (grid fins), engine hardware and high-temperature structure. The melt/mill tier is concentrated (VSMPO-AVISMA, ATI, TIMET) and was a documented 2022 supply-risk axis after Russian titanium exposure.
nodes.notes: Concentrated melt tier; VSMPO-AVISMA (Russia) is the world's largest producer and a post-2022 export-control corner for Western buyers. ATI and TIMET (PCC) are the principal Western merchant melters. SpaceX's specific Ti mill supplier for grid-fin stock is not publicly disclosed.

nodes.name: Titanium sponge feedstock
nodes.description: Titanium sponge — the upstream feedstock from which all aerospace mill titanium is melted. A near-single-geography corner: U.S. domestic sponge production has effectively ceased, leaving Western aerospace ~import-dependent, with Japan (Osaka Titanium, Toho Titanium) the principal merchant source plus PCC/TIMET in North America.
nodes.notes: Single/near-single-geography corner: U.S. Section 232 review found only one domestic sponge producer by 2019 and ~68% sponge import reliance; Japan's two producers (Osaka, Toho) plus PCC/TIMET dominate Western-accessible sponge. Feeds the mill-titanium tier above.

nodes.name: Large aerospace titanium forgings/castings (grid fins)
nodes.description: Large single-piece titanium castings/forgings for reusable-launch reentry-control surfaces — Falcon 9's hypersonic grid fins are cast in a single piece of titanium so they survive reentry heat without shielding and are reused without per-flight replacement. The titanium cast/forged-part tier (Howmet, PCC) is a recognized aerospace capacity chokepoint.
nodes.notes: CAPTIVE CORNER: Falcon 9's titanium grid fins are cast in a single piece of titanium by SpaceX (widely reported as among the largest single-piece Ti castings); no public merchant supplier of the grid-fin casting itself is named in reviewed sources, so no supplier is invented. The merchant exposure is the large-aero-Ti-forging/casting tier generally (Howmet, PCC), and the mill-Ti and sponge feedstock above. Quote support is for the captive single-piece casting fact, not a vendor.

nodes.name: Aerospace investment castings & forgings (engine/structure)
nodes.description: High-end aerospace investment castings and structural/rotating forgings feeding rocket engines and primary structure. A roughly $10B sector dominated by a two-supplier near-duopoly (Arconic/Howmet and Precision Castparts) that is a persistent, well-known capacity chokepoint for engine and airframe production.
nodes.notes: Near-duopoly capacity corner (Howmet + PCC). Industry-framed merchant tier feeding any rocket-engine/structure program; SpaceX additively manufactures many Raptor/Merlin hot-section parts in-house (captive) — the casting/forging duopoly is exposure for the broader engine-component class, not a confirmed SpaceX BOM line.

nodes.name: Constellium
nodes.description: Constellium SE — leading aerospace aluminium producer and maker of the proprietary Airware aluminium-lithium alloy used for launch-vehicle tank and structure components. Publicly supplies Airware Al-Li plate/sheet to Blue Origin's New Glenn; merchant Al-Li exposure for reusable-launch tankage.
nodes.notes: NYSE: CSTM (verified IR/exchange this round). Aerospace/space sites at Ravenswood, WV and Issoire, France. Airware Al-Li supplied to Blue Origin New Glenn (named launch program); not a confirmed Falcon 9 BOM supplier.

nodes.name: Kaiser Aluminum
nodes.description: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation — a leading producer of semi-fabricated specialty aluminum products with a major aerospace/high-strength plate and sheet business (Trentwood, WA mill). Merchant aero-aluminum exposure; second-source candidate for aerospace Al plate.
nodes.notes: NASDAQ: KALU (verified this round). FY2024 Aerospace/High-Strength net sales reported at $883M. Trentwood expansion adds ~25% heat-treat plate capacity. Aero plate supplier; not confirmed on Falcon 9/Starship BOM.

nodes.name: Arconic
nodes.description: Arconic Corporation — major rolled-aluminum and aerospace plate/sheet producer spun from Alcoa in 2016. One of the two leading aerospace casting/structures lineages historically (the other being PCC). Taken private by Apollo Global Management in 2023.
nodes.notes: PRIVATE since H2-2023: acquired by Apollo Global Management ($30.00/share), delisted from NYSE — no active public ticker (do not assign one). Distinct from Howmet Aerospace, which also spun from Alcoa/Arconic in 2020. Merchant aero-aluminum/castings lineage; not a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

nodes.name: VSMPO-AVISMA
nodes.description: VSMPO-AVISMA Corporation — the world's largest titanium producer and historically the largest titanium supplier to Boeing and Airbus. A post-2022 export-control / sanctions corner for Western aerospace titanium; Russia-based, ~25%+1 share held by state corporation Rostec.
nodes.notes: Trades on Moscow Exchange (VSMO); not accessible to most Western investors and exposed to post-2022 sanctions. Ownership: Industrial Investments (Mikhail Shelkov) ~65.27%, Rostec 25%+1 share. World's largest Ti producer; named largest Ti supplier for Boeing commercial production. Listed honestly as the export-control corner of the mill-Ti tier, NOT as a SpaceX supplier.

nodes.name: ATI Inc.
nodes.description: ATI Inc. (formerly Allegheny Technologies) — U.S. specialty-materials maker and a principal Western aerospace/defense titanium melter, also producing premium nickel mill products for engines. Expanding titanium melt ~35% and locking multi-year supply amid 'tight supply for critical materials'.
nodes.notes: NYSE: ATI (verified this round). Richland, WA melt expansion ~+35% over 2022 baseline; ~$1.2B aero/defense commitments. Merchant mill-Ti and Ni exposure; not a confirmed SpaceX BOM supplier.

nodes.name: TIMET (Titanium Metals Corp.)
nodes.description: TIMET (Titanium Metals Corporation) — integrated titanium producer (sponge, ingot, mill products) and, per its parent, the largest titanium sponge producer and melter in North America. Operated the last large U.S. sponge plant (Henderson, NV), idled since 2020. A subsidiary of Precision Castparts (Berkshire Hathaway).
nodes.notes: Subsidiary of Precision Castparts Corp. (PCC Metals Group Division), itself a Berkshire Hathaway company — public exposure only via BRK.B (parent ticker; TIMET/PCC have no standalone listing). Largest North American Ti sponge producer/melter. Held last large U.S. sponge plant (idled 2020). Upstream sponge + mill-Ti corner; not a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

nodes.name: Toho Titanium
nodes.description: Toho Titanium Co., Ltd. — one of Japan's two titanium-sponge producers (with Osaka Titanium). Together the Japanese sponge makers are the principal Western-accessible merchant source of aerospace titanium sponge feedstock as the West diversifies away from Russian supply.
nodes.notes: Tokyo Stock Exchange: 5727 (verified this round). One of only two Japanese sponge producers. NOTE: JX Advanced Metals (org_jx_advanced_metals, already in graph) announced (Feb 2026) taking Toho Titanium private via share exchange — listing status may change pending completion. Upstream sponge tier; not a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

nodes.name: Osaka Titanium Technologies
nodes.description: Osaka Titanium Technologies Co., Ltd. — the world's second-largest producer of titanium sponge after VSMPO-AVISMA, and one of Japan's two sponge producers. A core merchant source of aerospace titanium sponge feedstock for Western-accessible supply.
nodes.notes: Tokyo Stock Exchange: 5726 (verified this round). Named world's second-largest titanium sponge producer after VSMPO-AVISMA. Upstream sponge tier feeding mill-Ti; not a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

nodes.name: Howmet Aerospace
nodes.description: Howmet Aerospace Inc. — leading provider of advanced engineered aerospace components: investment castings, forgings, titanium mill products/extrusions and the #1 global position in aerospace fastening systems. States it can produce more than 90% of all structural and rotating aero-engine components. One of the two dominant aerospace casting/forging producers.
nodes.notes: NYSE: HWM (verified this round). #1 global in aerospace fastening systems; produces >90% of structural/rotating aero-engine component types; Engineered Structures makes titanium ingot, mill products and forgings. One of two dominant aero casting/forging firms (with PCC). Merchant castings/forgings/Ti exposure; not a confirmed SpaceX BOM supplier.

nodes.name: Precision Castparts Corp.
nodes.description: Precision Castparts Corp. (PCC) — worldwide diversified manufacturer of complex metal components: forgings, investment castings, fasteners and airframe products for aerospace. One of the two dominant aerospace investment-casting producers and, via TIMET, the largest titanium sponge producer/melter in North America. A Berkshire Hathaway company.
nodes.notes: Acquired by Berkshire Hathaway in 2016 — public exposure only via BRK.B (no standalone listing; do not assign a PCC ticker). One of two dominant aero casting/forging firms (with Howmet). Owns TIMET (Ti sponge/mill). Merchant castings/forgings/Ti exposure; not a confirmed SpaceX BOM supplier.

nodes.name: Outokumpu
nodes.description: Outokumpu Oyj — the largest stainless-steel producer in Europe and second-largest in the Americas. Publicly reported as a supplier of stainless steel to SpaceX for Starship; merchant 300-series stainless exposure for Starship primary structure.
nodes.notes: Nasdaq Helsinki: OUT1V (verified this round). Largest stainless producer in Europe, 2nd in the Americas (Calvert, AL operations). Reported as a SpaceX Starship stainless supplier (quality secondary source); 304L is a near-commodity grade with many qualified mills, so this is illustrative merchant exposure rather than a sole-source claim.

Constellium manufactures aerospace aluminum-lithium (Airware) plate/sheet for launch-vehicle structures and publicly supplies it to Blue Origin's New Glenn; merchant Al-Li exposure, not a confirmed Falcon 9 BOM claim.

Arconic is a major aerospace rolled-aluminum plate/sheet producer and capable supplier in the aero-aluminum tier; not confirmed as an Al-Li launch-tank supplier.
Falcon 9 titanium grid fins require aerospace mill titanium stock as their base material.
Falcon 9 grid fins require a large single-piece titanium casting/forging process.

Arconic is part of the historic aerospace castings/structures duopoly lineage and a capable supplier of aero structural parts; capability exposure, not a confirmed SpaceX BOM claim.

evidence.title: Constellium aerospace/space: aluminum-lithium for launch vehicles
evidence.summary: Constellium's space-market page lists aluminum-lithium plate/sheet/extrusions for launch-vehicle structural components, supporting Al-Li as the merchant material tier feeding reusable-launch tankage.
evidence.excerpt: We offer high-performance aluminum such, as aluminum-lithium alloys, in plate, sheet and extrusions for key structural components, including dome caps, barrel panels, stiffeners, intertanks, stage adapters / interstage structures, thrust structures, heat shields, and crew modules.
evidence.limitations: Vendor page; confirms Al-Li product for launch-vehicle structures and references 'Aluminum-Lithium on New Glenn' but does not prove a SpaceX/Falcon 9 BOM selection.

evidence.title: Constellium to supply Airware aluminium solutions to Blue Origin
evidence.summary: Constellium press release announcing supply of Airware aluminium plates and sheets for Blue Origin's New Glenn orbital launch vehicle — a direct reusable-launch-program Al-Li supply link.
evidence.excerpt: Under this agreement, Constellium is to supply Airware® aluminium plates and sheets for Blue Origin's massive orbital rocket, New Glenn.
evidence.limitations: Confirms Constellium Al-Li supply to a reusable-launch program (Blue Origin New Glenn), not to SpaceX specifically.

evidence.title: Constellium aluminium-lithium alloys (Airware) product page
evidence.summary: Constellium describes Airware as its proprietary aluminium-lithium solution developed over 20 years of R&D — supporting Constellium as a leading Al-Li producer.
evidence.excerpt: Airware®, Constellium's proprietary aluminum-lithium solution, delivers a breakthrough in material performance
evidence.limitations: Vendor product page; establishes proprietary Al-Li capability, weak for market-share quantification.

evidence.title: Kaiser Aluminum Q4/FY2024 results — aerospace/high-strength business
evidence.summary: Kaiser Aluminum's FY2024 results describe it as a leading producer of semi-fabricated specialty aluminum products serving aerospace and high-strength applications.
evidence.excerpt: a leading producer of semi-fabricated specialty aluminum products serving customers worldwide with highly-engineered solutions for aerospace and high-strength
evidence.limitations: Confirms Kaiser as a leading aero/high-strength aluminum producer; does not establish Al-Li launch-tank supply or a SpaceX relationship.

evidence.excerpt: increase in heat treat plate production capacity by approximately 25%

evidence.summary: Boeing press release identifying VSMPO-AVISMA as the largest titanium supplier for Boeing commercial production, used on multiple Boeing models — establishing VSMPO-AVISMA as the dominant aerospace mill-titanium producer.
evidence.excerpt: VSMPO-AVISMA is the largest titanium supplier for Boeing commercial production.
evidence.limitations: Establishes VSMPO-AVISMA dominance in aerospace titanium (Boeing context, pre-2022). Not a SpaceX supply claim; recorded as the export-control concentration of the mill-Ti tier.

evidence.sourceName: ATI Inc. Investor Relations (company press release)

evidence.excerpt: The expansion will increase ATI's production of aerospace and defense-grade titanium by approximately 35% over the 2022 baseline levels
evidence.limitations: Capacity-expansion figure for ATI aerospace/defense titanium; not specific to launch or SpaceX.

evidence.limitations: Summary of a government report (not the primary doc); establishes U.S. sponge near-monopoly/import-reliance, not a SpaceX claim.

evidence.title: Falcon 9 titanium grid fins cast in a single piece (2017)
evidence.summary: Spaceflight Now report (citing Elon Musk) that Falcon 9's upgraded titanium grid fins are cast in a single piece of titanium and survive reentry heat without shielding — establishing the captive single-piece Ti casting.
evidence.excerpt: He added that the grid fins are cast in a single piece of titanium and cut to form their shape.
evidence.limitations: Establishes the single-piece Ti casting (SpaceX-captive process); does not name a merchant supplier of the grid-fin casting (none invented).

evidence.title: Aerospace castings a 'well-known choke point'; Arconic/PCC duopoly
evidence.summary: Aviation Week reporting that aerospace investment castings are a persistent capacity chokepoint dominated by two providers — Arconic and Precision Castparts.
evidence.excerpt: The aerospace castings sector, a roughly $10 billion industry, is dominated by two leading providers: Arconic and Precision Castparts (PCC).
evidence.limitations: Names Arconic and PCC as the dominant two; Howmet (Engine Products/Engineered Products) is the engine-casting successor lineage to Arconic's casting business. Sector-size figure is for aerospace castings broadly, not launch-specific.

evidence.title: Howmet Aerospace — >90% of structural/rotating aero-engine components
evidence.summary: Howmet states it can produce more than 90 percent of all structural and rotating aero-engine components, including investment castings, forgings and titanium products.
evidence.excerpt: We can produce more than 90 percent of all structural and rotating aero engine components
evidence.limitations: Vendor claim about engine-component breadth; not a market-share figure and not a SpaceX-specific claim.

evidence.title: Howmet Aerospace — number one global position in aerospace fastening systems
evidence.summary: Howmet states it holds the number one global position in aerospace fastening systems — supporting concentrated supplier position in a structural-metals component class.
evidence.excerpt: We hold the number one global position in aerospace fastening systems
evidence.limitations: Vendor claim of #1 position in fasteners (a related structural-metals class); not quantified share and not launch-specific.

evidence.title: Precision Castparts Corp. — about (complex metal components; Berkshire; TIMET)
evidence.summary: PCC about page describing it as a worldwide diversified manufacturer of complex metal components for aerospace, acquired by Berkshire Hathaway, with TIMET as its titanium operation.
evidence.excerpt: Precision Castparts Corp. is a worldwide, diversified manufacturer of complex metal components and products.
evidence.limitations: Vendor about page; establishes PCC's aerospace component manufacturing and Berkshire/TIMET ownership. Not a SpaceX-specific claim.

evidence.title: Outokumpu supplies SpaceX with stainless steel for Starship
evidence.summary: Secondary report stating Outokumpu supplies SpaceX with stainless steel for Starship, in the context of Outokumpu also supplying Tesla — supporting Outokumpu as a merchant stainless supplier to the Starship structure.
evidence.excerpt: It's worth noting that Outokumpu also supplies SpaceX with stainless steel for Starship.
evidence.limitations: Quality secondary source (not primary/IR); confirms the supply relationship but not grade, volume, or exclusivity. 304L is a near-commodity grade with many qualified mills — illustrative merchant exposure, not sole-source.

evidence.title: Starship stainless: 304L near-commodity, SpaceX moving to in-house 30X alloy
evidence.summary: Report quoting Musk that 304-class stainless is abundant ('what they make pots out of'), that some parts use 304L for cryo toughness, and that SpaceX would move to internally developed alloys — supporting the 304L near-commodity note and the captive 30X alloy direction.
evidence.excerpt: 304 stainless is what they make pots out of. There's plenty of it.
evidence.limitations: Secondary blog quoting Musk; supports the near-commodity character of 304-series stainless and SpaceX's stated move to internally developed (captive) alloys (30X). Not used for any quantified market claim.

evidence.title: SpaceX Starship stainless steel: 301 to 304 to proprietary 30X
evidence.summary: BSSA article describing SpaceX's stainless progression from 301 to 304 and ultimately to a proprietary 30X alloy — supporting the captive-alloy honesty note for Starship primary structure.
evidence.excerpt: SpaceX started with stainless steel 301 but moved to 304 and ultimately developed its proprietary alloy, 30X, which surpassed the performance of both 301 and 304.
evidence.limitations: Industry-association article; supports the proprietary 30X (captive) direction. Not used for a quantified market claim.
